# TomlScalarError

Why a scalar could not be read, and where in it.

```rux
pub variant TomlScalarError {
    Malformed(uint),
    OutOfRange(uint),
    TooLong(uint)
}
```

Failure-only: there is no case meaning nothing went wrong, because a scalar that read hands back its value
instead. Every offset is a zero-based byte offset into the scalar's own text, as the caller wrote it —
underscores included — and reachable through `Text::ParseFailure`.

## Cases

| Name               | Description                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          |
| ------------------ | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `Malformed(uint)`  | The text does not have the shape TOML defines, at the byte carried. That is the first character that cannot be part of what was being read: a digit the base does not have, a point with nothing after it, an underscore that is not between two digits, or the end of the text when it stops early. |
| `OutOfRange(uint)` | The value is outside what an `int64`, a `float64` or the calendar can hold. The offset is the start of the text, since it is the whole value that does not fit rather than any one character of it.                                                                                                  |
| `TooLong(uint)`    | The text is longer than any TOML scalar needs. The offset is the first character past the bound.                                                                                                                                                                                                     |

## Implements ParseFailure

`TomlScalarError` conforms to `ParseFailure`.

<h3 id="offset"><code>Offset</code></h3>

```rux
pub func Offset(self: &TomlScalarError) -> uint
```

Where in the scalar's text the failure was found.
Borrows the failure and leaves it untouched. Cannot fail; runs in constant time and allocates nothing.

**Returns**: the zero-based byte offset into the scalar's own text

[Source](https://github.com/rux-lang/Rux/blob/main/Packages/Toml/Src/Scalar.rux#L43)

## Implements Display

`TomlScalarError` conforms to `Display`.

<h3 id="write-display"><code>WriteDisplay</code></h3>

```rux
pub func WriteDisplay(
    self: &TomlScalarError,
    writer: &var TextWriter,
    spec: FormatSpec
) -> ! FormatError
```

Writes the description of why the scalar could not be read, without the position.
The offset is a number a caller places where it makes sense for them — beside a line and column, or not at
all — so it is not written into the middle of a sentence here. `Debug` carries it.
Reports whatever the writer reported, and `UnsupportedRequest` for any style or precision.

| Name     | Type              | Description                    |
| -------- | ----------------- | ------------------------------ |
| `writer` | `&var TextWriter` | the destination                |
| `spec`   | `FormatSpec`      | what the placeholder asked for |

**Returns**: success when the whole description was accepted

[Source](https://github.com/rux-lang/Rux/blob/main/Packages/Toml/Src/Scalar.rux#L61)
